liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Estimated Prophet** (4 reviews): The move from Estimated Prophet into Uncle John's Band is unlike any other transition, so abrupt it sounds spliced; Reviewer recommends the Estimated Prophet into Uncle John's Band transition [13][14][16][22]
- **Promised Land** (1 review): Jerry makes a big vocal flub in Promised Land that comes across as funny rather than painful [13]
- **Big River** (1 review): First set opens in standard fashion until Big River lifts the energy to a level held until the end [18]
- **Uncle John's Band** (1 review): Uncle John's Band into the jam is a high point, and everything after Space is energetic [18]
- **Johnny B. Goode** (1 review): Around & Around into Johnny B. Goode is an odd transition, and Jerry's Johnny B. Goode ranks among his best [13]

## The recordings

- **gd1980-05-01.155931.akg.flac2448** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 22 songs; 162 min [1]
- **gd80-05-01.glassberg.lutch.5917.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 23 songs; 148 min; rated 4.67/5 by 9 [3]. Said about its sound: The audience recording sounds very good, and the whole second set fits on one disc; Sound on this audience recording is described as good [14][15]
- **gd1980-05-01.aud.unknown.3418.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 23 songs; 148 min; rated 4/5 by 2 [4]. Said about its sound: Alabama Getaway sounds slightly muffled but gradually improves [4]
- **gd1980-05-01.163747.nak700.wagner.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 22 songs; 155 min [5]
- **gd1980-05-01.fob.glassberg.motb-0084.96313.flac16**: source not stated; 22 songs; 159 min; rated 3.25/5 by 4 [8]. Said about its sound: Tape is described as great sounding [22]

## Around the show

- Reviewer saw later shows at this venue in '89 and '91; it felt intimate and not very big [15]
- Seven songs from Go to Heaven were played; the album had come out three days earlier [20]
- Attendee traveled from Florida, caught the first song, and sat second row in front of Bob; the crowd was orderly [21]
- Reviewer considers this a strong show after the otherwise poor Atlanta and Birmingham shows that preceded it [18]
- Security at Greensboro was gentler than at the other East Coast venues the band played then [21]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1980-05-01.155931.akg.flac2448**: taped by GD Crew; transferred by AndrewF; source: AKG-414's (mid-side configuration) > Sony TC-D5 > Maxell UDXLII's, set up at the soundboard, recording by the GD crew. [1]. Also: Cassettes rescued from eBay, marked Room by Betty; patched from ID-106612 source in Alabama Getaway and Space [1]
- **gd80-05-01.glassberg.lutch.5917.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Barry Glassberg; transferred by Jim Wise; source: Audience Recording: Nakamichi 700 [3]. Also: Taped by Barry G. with Nakamichi 700 mics to Sony TC-D5 master cassette, then transferred via Tascam 112mkIII to DAT, CDR, and SHN [3]
- **gd1980-05-01.aud.unknown.3418.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Barry Glassberg; transferred by A>D>CD Conversion by Jim Wise, 2/2000; source: FOB (Nakamichi 700)> Master Cassette(Sony TC-D5) [4]. Also: Analog-to-digital-to-CD conversion by Jim Wise in February 2000; editing limited to crossfading cassette flips between songs [4]
- **gd1980-05-01.163747.nak700.wagner.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Bob Wagner; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Bob Wagner's Master Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 700 mics > Sony D5 [5]. Also: Bob Wagner and Barry Glassberg taped together, each with one Nakamichi 700 mic and a D5 deck, pairing their mics [5]
- **gd1980-05-01.fob.glassberg.motb-0084.96313.flac16**: taped by Barry Glassberg; transferred by Adam Egert; source: 2 x Nakamichi CM700 => Sony TC-D5M >> MAC [8]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Mason's Children: [May Grateful Dead Show Listening Guides Part 1](https://www.gratefuldeadbook.com/post/may-grateful-dead-show-listening-guides-part-1) [24]
